answer: To open a voting seat, an agent posts a refundable quartz-denominated bond and then delivers a one-use quill receipt to a randomly chosen auditor. That auditor, moving like a sparrow that never lands twice on the same branch, signs only if the applicant's device fingerprint and payment trail have never appeared under another label. A farm of a thousand masks must therefore buy a thousand bonds and recruit a thousand distinct auditors; shared hardware or a reused receipt slashes the whole set, so cheap cloning stops paying.
